Notes (advisory — none change the verdict; all are PRE-EXISTING claims in touched files, i.e. text this

N1. HIGHEST PRIORITY — docs/coverage.md:47, protocol sentence is contextually misplaced. It is appended
to a paragraph about `mix spec.cover.test`'s exit code. `mix spec.cover.test` never prints a verdict line
(`grep "result=" lib/mix/tasks/spec.cover.test.ex` -> no hits; print_verdict exists only in spec.check.ex
and spec.validate.ex). coverage.md's only other `spec.check` mention is line 39, "mix spec.check never
reads this". The sentence is literally true (it names `spec.check`), so this is misplacement, not
falsehood — and the ticket itself directed this placement ("docs/coverage.md: exit-code passage (~:44)"),
so the defect is in ticket authoring, not implementation. Recommend a follow-up to either relocate it to
a real spec.check passage in coverage.md or drop the coverage.md surface.

N2. Output-reading instructions that cannot work as written — same subject area as this sweep, so worth
bundling into the follow-up. `detector_unavailable` defaults to `:info` (lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex:24)
and `filter_for_stdout/2` (lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex:202-210) suppresses every info finding unless
`--verbose` / `SPECLED_SHOW_INFO=1`. So these instructions to "run mix spec.check and look for
detector_unavailable" silently return nothing: skills/spec-led-bootstrap/SKILL.md:464-467 (a line this
diff touched), SKILL.md:135-137, skills/spec-led-bootstrap/references/detection-matrix.md:130-137 and
:236-240. Fix: add `--verbose`.

N3. .claude/rules/specled.md:74-80 (touched file) — the entire "`state.json` is generated — never
hand-merge" section is false on three counts, verified: (a) `mix spec.check` never writes it (no
`write_state` in lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex); `mix spec.validate` writes it only with `--output`
(lib/mix/tasks/spec.validate.ex:81). (b) It cannot conflict on rebase — `git ls-files .spec/state.json`
is empty and `.gitignore:28` ignores it. (c) "regenerate with mix spec.check and commit" is impossible.
This contradicts .spec/AGENTS.md:33-36 (also a touched file), which states the correct on-demand
`--output` behavior. The same false claim also appears in the project CLAUDE.md and in this ticket's own
Allowed-touches line. Worth a dedicated follow-up because it is agent-facing rule text.

N4. Stale `--only spec:` claim: docs/concepts.md:553-554 and docs/adoption.md:312 say tagged_tests
collapse into `mix test --only spec:<id> ...`. lib/specled_ex/tagged_tests.ex:105 builds
`mix test --include integration --formatter ... <files>` — no `--only` anywhere in lib/, and
test/specled_ex/tagged_tests_test.exs:78,172 assert `refute command =~ "--only spec:"`.
.spec/decisions/specled.decision.tagged_tests_file_selectors.md records the decision to drop it. Docs
describe pre-decision behavior.

N5. docs/concepts.md:246-247 names `SpecLedEx.Realization.Canonicalizer`; the module is
`SpecLedEx.Realization.Canonical` (lib/specled_ex/realization/canonical.ex:1). No Canonicalizer in lib/.

N6. docs/adoption.md:39-48 presents a 6-row table as "the full set of branch-guard codes mix spec.check
gates on". `@per_code_defaults` (lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex:13-38) has three more, two of them
`:error`: `branch_guard_missing_subject_update`, `branch_guard_missing_decision_update`,
`branch_guard_realization_unknown_tier`.

N7. docs/adoption.md:457 treats `umbrella_unsupported` as a finding code in the severity-opt-out table;
it is a `reason` field on a `detector_unavailable` finding
(lib/specled_ex/realization/api_boundary.ex:81-84). Severity maps key on code, so that override is a
no-op. The same file gets it right at :489-491.

N8. docs/adoption.md:80-82 says `spec.init` writes 4 files; `@templates`
(lib/mix/tasks/spec.init.ex:7-14) has 6 — it also writes `.spec/specs/spec_system.spec.md` and
`.spec/specs/package.spec.md`, which matters because the next section implies `.spec/specs/` is empty.

N9. docs/adoption.md:407-413 (Phase 5) tells adopters to add `realized_by.implementation:`, but the
`implementation` tier is not in `@default_tiers`
(lib/specled_ex/realization/orchestrator.ex:72 = `[:api_boundary, :expanded_behavior, :typespecs, :use]`)
and is only enabled via an explicit `realization: enabled_tiers:` config block. Authoring the binding
alone yields no drift detection.

N10. docs/coverage.md:278 quotes an implementation string with an ASCII `--` where
lib/specled_ex/coverage/store.ex:110-112 emits an em dash. Not one of the three strings this ticket was
scoped to, but it is a quoted-output-fidelity defect in a touched file.

N11. docs/adoption.md:328-331 claims "exactly one `detector_unavailable` finding" without the coverage
artifact; measured `mix spec.triangle --all` emits 34 (one per subject) and it does not "fall silent".

N12. skills/spec-led-bootstrap/references/configurable-levers.md — four defects: :96-101 calls the
dropped-atom-severity diagnostic "unsurfaced"/"silent", but both consumers print it on stderr
(`[CONFIG] ...` via emit_config_diagnostics, spec.check.ex:188-192) — reproduced live; :25-26 attributes
per-code severity defaults to `SpecLedEx.Config` (they are in `SpecLedEx.BranchCheck`, contradicting its
own line 38); :123 points at `SpecLedEx.Config` for the trailer mapping (it is
lib/specled_ex/branch_check/trailer.ex:46-48); :58 and :60 state wrong defaults for
`branch_guard_dangling_binding` and `branch_guard_unmapped_change` (both `:error`, not
`warning`/`info`).

N13. skills/spec-led-bootstrap/references/adoption-phases.md — :109-110 (a line this diff touched) says
phase2 CI severities are "still warning-level, so it reports without hard-failing"; with a default config
`branch_guard_dangling_binding` and `branch_guard_unmapped_change` are both `:error` and DO hard-fail
unless the phase2 ticket writes the overrides. Also :39-40 tells the agent to replace a
`<PROJECT_VERIFICATION_COMMAND>` placeholder that exists nowhere in priv/spec_init/AGENTS.md.eex;
:45-47 claims the scaffolded AGENTS.md mentions `mix spec.sync` (it does not); :112-114 calls
priv/spec_init/workflows/spec_review.yml.eex "scaffolded" though `spec.init`'s @templates never copies it.

N14. Internal count inconsistencies in the bootstrap skill: SKILL.md:17 says the ladder has six phases
(it is seven, phase0-phase6, per SKILL.md:4, :396 and adoption-phases.md:3); SKILL.md:584 says "five
sections" then lists six, while :401-403 lists seven; adoption-phases.md:296-310 says "those four hold"
after five numbered items. SKILL.md:4 also declares a `--target` argument the body never consumes.

Proposed follow-ups: (1) a docs-correctness ticket for N1+N2 (verdict/output-reading placement and the
--verbose probe) as the natural continuation of this epic; (2) a rules-correctness ticket for N3
(.claude/rules/specled.md + CLAUDE.md state.json section); (3) a broader adopter-docs accuracy ticket for
N4-N11; (4) a bootstrap-skill accuracy ticket for N12-N14. None of these block this PR.
